title: BSW.DevSpark Knowledge Ontology
description: Authoritative machine-readable vocabulary for the Knowledge supply contract. Tooling, schemas, and prompts read this instead of restating the lists independently; a contract test proves it stays synchronized with build_knowledge_index.py, entity-node.schema.json, and taxonomy-registry.schema.json.

forms.description: Structural kind of a Knowledge artifact: what the artifact IS. Derived, never authored and never assignable by the taxonomy registry.

values.flat-document: A standalone Knowledge document under .knowledge/ that is not part of an entity.
values.entity-layer: A facet document under .knowledge/entities/<id>/ describing one layer of an entity.

determination.rule: Form is computed from artifact location and filename. Frontmatter may restate the resulting form but may not select it; a declared form that contradicts structure is a build error.
precedence: 2. recognized governance-decision location (.knowledge/governance/decisions/), excluding navigational filenames
determination.navigationRule: A file that indexes a directory is navigation, not a member of it. This is why .knowledge/governance/decisions/README.md is a flat-document rather than a decision, and it depends on the filename rather than on anything the document claims about itself.

roles.description: The kind of truth an artifact carries: what the artifact SAYS. Each form draws its role from its own domain; no role name was invented for 7.8-A.

flat-document.source: explicit frontmatter `type`, otherwise the taxonomy registry, otherwise authoritative-reference

roles.taxonomyResolution: Most specific matching pattern wins regardless of declaration order. A repository mapping outranks a built-in default only as a tiebreak at equal specificity. Two same-origin mappings of equal specificity that disagree are ambiguous and fail loudly.

canonicalFields.description: Which field a consumer MUST read for each concept. No 7.8 code should have to decide which meaning of `type` was intended.

form.compatibility: node.type, when the node is not a flat document

role.compatibility: node.type, when the node is a flat document
role.newAuthorsUse: frontmatter `type` on flat documents; `layer` on entity layers

entityType.compatibility: entity.type - unchanged, it was never overloaded

entityTypes.description: Controlled semantic classification for an entity. Advisory: an entity type never requires a layer to exist.

values.subsystem: An internal capability of the system this repository builds.
values.domain: A business/problem-space concept whose rules originate outside the code.
values.integration: A boundary with an external system, protocol, or third-party service.
values.tooling: Developer-facing automation that supports delivery rather than being shipped.

unknownType.rule: If evidence supports a concept but no entity type can be chosen confidently, the entity is not materialized. There is no fallback type. The concept may still exist as a discovery proposal or as flat Knowledge; what is blocked is minting an authoritative entity, not recognizing the idea.

extensibility.rule: The vocabulary is closed to tools and open to deliberate schema change. No tool may invent a type at runtime.
requirementsToAdd: repository evidence that the concept recurs
a semantic distinction no existing type already carries
no overlap with an existing type
schema update here and in entity-node.schema.json
contract tests covering the new value

entityTypes.layerIndependence: Entity type and entity-layer role are independent axes that happen to share the name `integration`. An entity may BE a boundary (type=integration) or merely HAVE an integration facet (layer=integration). Neither implies the other.

claimKinds.description: How a Knowledge artifact may reference a repository path. The two are never interchangeable: only ownership participates in ownership-overlap analysis.

values.source_of_truth: Evidence ownership - artifacts that materially implement, prove, or constrain this Knowledge, such that changing them may make it stale.
values.appliesTo: Applicability scope - where this Knowledge governs, applies, or must be considered. Not ownership.

claimKinds.ownershipTest: If this source changed materially, could this Knowledge become stale or incorrect? If no, it is not source_of_truth.
eligibleAsOwnership: test source that materially proves or constrains the documented behavior
ineligibleAsOwnership: files that merely mention the concept
claimKinds.multipleOwners: Not invalid. A genuinely cross-cutting file may implement more than one concept, so two owners is surfaced for review rather than prohibited.

entityModel.relationships: Semantic relationships belong to the entity, authored as `relations` in _entity.yaml. An entity layer may not author them; `links` on a layer is a build error rather than an ignored field.
entityModel.hasLayer: The entity -> layer edge is framework-derived composition, not an authored semantic relation.
entityModel.layerIdentity: A layer describes one facet of its parent entity and has no independent conceptual identity. It may carry aliases, because aliases are a retrieval affordance rather than graph identity.
entityModel.flatVersusEntity: Flat Knowledge is the default. An entity exists only when a durable concept benefits from multiple independently useful facets, graph identity, or distinct ownership and drift accounting. File count and directory spread are evidence, never justification on their own.

integrityFindings.meaning: A finding represents a condition that deserves current attention.
integrityFindings.acceptedOverride: A valid authored role that differs from a broad taxonomy glob is the precedence rule working as designed, and is not a finding.
integrityFindings.contradiction: A valid authored role that differs from an exact-path taxonomy mapping is two deliberate statements disagreeing about one file, and is a finding.

compatibility.typeField: Pre-7.8 consumers read a single `type` field. It is retained with its exact historical values - the role for a flat document, the form otherwise - and is compatibility-only. On a flat document an authored `type` means role and nothing else; it carries no structural meaning. `form` and `role` are canonical.
